content.text:
I've written a Go reimplementation of Miller 6.16.0 (`mlr`), built only from running the provided binary and reading its own help output. Everything is committed and a fresh clone builds cleanly with `./compile.sh`. Some edge cases still differ from the original (listed below).

**How I checked it:** I ran the same commands through the original and my build and compared stdout and exit codes. Hand-written suites cover formats, verbs, DSL features, emit variants and help output. Several randomly generated batches of 600 multi-verb commands each passed 600/600 by the end. Random DSL-expression batches of 500 still had 2–3 failures each, all on odd type combinations. Every verb's `--help`, and the help for every function and keyword, matched byte-for-byte. stderr text was not compared, only exit codes.

**What's covered:**
- **Formats:** DKVP, NIDX, CSV, TSV and their "lite" forms, JSON, JSON Lines, XTAB, PPRINT (barred and right-aligned), Markdown, USV/ASV, plus approximate YAML and DCF. Most flags, separator aliases, comment handling, gzip/bz2 input, `--ofmt`, `-n`, `--from` and `-I` in-place editing work.
- **Verbs:** every verb in `mlr help list-verbs`, including stats1/stats2, merge-fields, step, top, nest, reshape, join, summary, sort and split. Seeded `sample`, `shuffle`, `bootstrap` and `urand*` reproduce the original's random sequences.
- **DSL:** a full parser (`put -v` tree output matches), about 230 built-in functions, user functions and subroutines, all emit/tee/print/dump variants with file redirects, and the original's number formatting and type-mixing rules.
- **Original quirks kept on purpose:**
  - `strlen` of a number returns `(error)`.
  - `&=` behaves as XOR.
  - A `filter false` inside `put` keeps dropping all later records.
  - Records emitted at end of stream by `fraction` see the final `NR`.

**Known differences:**
- `put -d` / `-D` (parenthesised syntax tree) output is only approximate.
- `stats2 -a logireg` differs in the last digits.
- `strptime` with a time-only format: the original returns an odd year-1753 value; mine doesn't.
- DSL parse-error messages leave out the "Expected one of:" token list. Exit code is still 1.

I've written a Go reimplementation of Miller 6.16.0 (`mlr`), built only from running the provided binary and reading its own help output. Everything is committed and a fresh clone builds cleanly with `./compile.sh`. Some edge cases still differ from the original (listed below).

**How I checked it:** I ran the same commands through the original and my build and compared stdout and exit codes. Hand-written suites cover formats, verbs, DSL features, emit variants and help output. Several randomly generated batches of 600 multi-verb commands each passed 600/600 by the end. Random DSL-expression batches of 500 still had 2–3 failures each, all on odd type combinations. Every verb's `--help`, and the help for every function and keyword, matched byte-for-byte. stderr text was not compared, only exit codes.

**What's covered:**
- **Formats:** DKVP, NIDX, CSV, TSV and their "lite" forms, JSON, JSON Lines, XTAB, PPRINT (barred and right-aligned), Markdown, USV/ASV, plus approximate YAML and DCF. Most flags, separator aliases, comment handling, gzip/bz2 input, `--ofmt`, `-n`, `--from` and `-I` in-place editing work.
- **Verbs:** every verb in `mlr help list-verbs`, including stats1/stats2, merge-fields, step, top, nest, reshape, join, summary, sort and split. Seeded `sample`, `shuffle`, `bootstrap` and `urand*` reproduce the original's random sequences.
- **DSL:** a full parser (`put -v` tree output matches), about 230 built-in functions, user functions and subroutines, all emit/tee/print/dump variants with file redirects, and the original's number formatting and type-mixing rules.
- **Original quirks kept on purpose:**
  - `strlen` of a number returns `(error)`.
  - `&=` behaves as XOR.
  - A `filter false` inside `put` keeps dropping all later records.
  - Records emitted at end of stream by `fraction` see the final `NR`.

**Known differences:**
- `put -d` / `-D` (parenthesised syntax tree) output is only approximate.
- `stats2 -a logireg` differs in the last digits.
- `strptime` with a time-only format: the original returns an odd year-1753 value; mine doesn't.
- DSL parse-error messages leave out the "Expected one of:" token list. Exit code is still 1.
- Writing CSV with mismatched columns to a file from inside `put` (e.g. `tee >` or `emit >`) makes the original hang (it timed out in my tests). Mine exits with an error instead.
- `concat` and `append` with absent arguments: the original prints an internal error; mine doesn't.
- No timezone data exists on this machine and the original doesn't bundle any, so I deliberately didn't either. Named-timezone functions fail the same way the original does here.
- A few unusual type combinations in built-in functions may still differ.

The workspace `./executable` is still the original binary; `compile.sh` overwrites it with the new build. These gaps are also listed in `AGENT_REPORT.md`.
